## Methods (mysterycall_methods_paragraph)

A mystery-caller audit methodology was employed. A total of 731 physicians representing General, Facial Plastics, Head and Neck Cancer, Laryngology, Otology/neurotology, Pediatrics, Rhinology and Sleep were identified from publicly available directories across 468 cities and states in the United States. Mystery callers posed as new patients insured with  and contacted each physician's office to request the earliest available new-patient appointment. Calls were standardized and completed within one week of each other. The primary outcome was business days until the next available new-patient appointment. All analyses were performed using R 4.4.2. A multilevel negative binomial regression model with physician random intercepts was fit using the glmmTMB package to account for overdispersion in appointment wait times and estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR).

## Results

### Access (mysterycall_results_paragraph, subject overridden)

Facial Plastics requested-subspecialty calls were 10% less likely to be offered an appointment (OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.54-1.52, p=0.696). Head and Neck Cancer requested-subspecialty calls were 17% less likely to be offered an appointment (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.36-1.91, p=0.661). Laryngology requested-subspecialty calls were 74% more likely to be offered an appointment (OR 1.74, 95% CI 0.50-6.08, p=0.385). Otology/neurotology requested-subspecialty calls were 51% less likely to be offered an appointment (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.23-1.07, p=0.074). Pediatrics requested-subspecialty calls were 126% more likely to be offered an appointment (OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.08-4.75, p=0.031). Rhinology requested-subspecialty calls were 111% more likely to be offered an appointment (OR 2.11, 95% CI 0.72-6.17, p=0.174). Sleep requested-subspecialty calls were 66% more likely to be offered an appointment (OR 1.66, 95% CI 0.55-5.03, p=0.371).

### Timeliness — descriptive (mysterycall_wait_time_sentence)

The median wait time across all rural was 14 business days (IQR: 5–30). Specifically, the median wait time was 13 days (IQR: 5–31) for Urban, 20 days (IQR: 4–40) for Rural, 14 days (IQR: 6–26) for Suburban. The p-value for Rural vs Urban was 0.114. The p-value for Suburban vs Urban was < 0.001.

### Timeliness — dispersion (mysterycall_overdispersion_sentence)

The Pearson dispersion ratio is 0.72 (chi-square = 295.54, df = 408, p = 1.000). No significant overdispersion detected (ratio = 0.72). The Poisson model appears adequate.

### Timeliness clustering (mysterycall_icc_sentence, wait model)

The intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.063 (6.3% of variance attributable to between-physician clustering), justifying the use of a multilevel model.
